title: MCP (Model Context Protocol): how agents reach tools, and where you can stop them
summary: Hold: the licensing guidance would lead administrators to budget for premium licences that the cited service description no longer requires for tenant-wide tool control. Microsoft now lists that control as included with a Microsoft cloud subscription. The control paths and automation otherwise check out, with several paths stopping before the final control.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP policy page says mutation operations are not allowed by default and can be enabled through tenant policy.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. ... Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.where: Open questions: Work IQ write defaults
claims.claim: Copilot Studio's what's-new page says Work IQ write operations are enabled by default in that product.
claims.quote: now added by default to every new agent powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness ... Write operations are enabled by default, subject to your organization's permissions and policies.
claims.fix: Replace the second clause with: 'the Copilot Studio what's-new page says Work IQ write operations are enabled by default for new agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, subject to the organisation's permissions and policies.'

claims.claim: Dataverse Web API PATCH applies a JSON object's properties to the URI representing an individual record.
claims.quote: Update operations use the HTTP PATCH verb. Pass a JSON object containing the properties you want to update to the URI that represents the record.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/update-delete-entities-using-web-api to sources for the individual-record PATCH syntax used by controls[9].api; keep its existing allowedmcpclient reference link.
